payload.prompt_text: You are writing the terms for a guided walk. Nothing cancels it except a formal weather warning. Write one sentence that says so, and make sure a reader could not mistake it for a warning about ordinary rain.

feedback.why_key: Terms are read by people who will hold you to them, so the exact weight of the condition is the whole sentence.
feedback.feed_forward: Name the one exception and nothing else.

parts: A local paper is thinking about charging for its website.
Most readers say they would pay a small amount.
The paper loses money on print whatever happens online.
model_combinations: Even if every reader paid for the website, the paper would still be losing money on the printed edition.
The print losses continue even if the website starts charging, so the charge cannot be the whole answer.
Unless the printed edition is dealt with as well, a charge on the website will not save the paper.

feedback.why_key: The third fact is the one that decides the connecting word, because it says the condition cannot change the outcome on its own.
feedback.feed_forward: Let the fact that decides nothing take even if.

payload.prompt_text: Return to your letter about the bus service. Rewrite the sentence that says what would settle the matter, so that it names one exception rather than a list of demands. Two minutes.

feedback.why_key: A complaint that names one thing which would settle it is far harder to ignore than one that lists everything that has gone wrong.
feedback.feed_forward: State the single condition that would close the matter.

points.title: Saying that things are not how you want them, and nudging them along

point_json.grammar_name: wish, if only, it's time, would rather

teach.can_do: I can say that something is not as I want it, and that I would like somebody to change it.
teach.why_it_matters: Speaking keeps asking what you would change about your home, your town or a decision. These frames are the ready-made answers, and they cost almost nothing now.
teach.meaning: Four frames, one mechanism. Each of them takes the backward step you have just learned and points it at a different kind of gap. Wish with a stepped-back verb says a state is not as you want it. Wish with would says somebody else keeps doing something and you want them to stop. Wish with had says a moment went by unused. It's time and would rather turn the same step into a nudge and a preference.

form.pattern: wish / if only + one step back  ·  it's (high) time + a stepped-back verb  ·  would rather + you + a stepped-back verb
notes: About a state now: I wish the flat had more storage.
About somebody else's habit that you want stopped: I wish the neighbours would shut the gate.
About a moment that has gone: I wish I had taken the ground-floor one.
If only is the same three shapes with more heat behind them.
Would rather takes a plain verb when the person stays the same (I'd rather walk) and a stepped-back verb when it changes (I'd rather you walked).
form.negative: The step survives a negative untouched: I wish the hallway didn't smell of damp.
form.question: Would you rather we met at the station or at the hall?

steps.gloss: a state: it is broken and that is how things are

steps.text: I wish they would fix the lift
steps.gloss: somebody else's behaviour: they could act and they are not acting

steps.text: I wish I had reported it sooner
steps.gloss: a moment gone: the chance came and went unused

steps.text: It's time somebody fixed the lift
steps.gloss: a nudge: nobody has started and the speaker is out of patience

worked_example.sentence: I wish the people upstairs would move the bikes out of the hallway.
worked_example.why_this_form: Would points at somebody else's repeated behaviour and asks for it to change. The speaker cannot move the bikes and is not pretending to be able to.
worked_example.what_the_other_would_mean: I wish the people upstairs moved the bikes would report the hallway as a settled fact of the building, closer to describing a house style than to asking anyone to do anything about it.

notice_set.sentence: I wish the boiler heated the whole flat.
notice_set.question: Does the boiler heat the whole flat?
notice_set.why: The backward step is the speaker's way of saying that the heat does not reach everywhere.

notice_set.sentence: I wish I had looked at the flat in winter.
notice_set.question: Did the speaker see the flat in winter?
notice_set.why: Two steps back reaches a chance that came and went, and reports it as one nobody took.

notice_set.sentence: I wish the man downstairs would move his bike out of the hallway.
notice_set.question: Whose action is the speaker waiting on?
notice_set.why: Would puts the ball in somebody else's court: the speaker is asking, not planning.

notice_set.sentence: It's about time the council emptied the bins on this street.
notice_set.question: Have the bins been emptied?
notice_set.why: The step back says the emptying has not happened, and the sentence exists to complain about that.

notice_set.sentence: I'd rather you didn't give the door code to anyone.
notice_set.question: Does the speaker want the code shared?
notice_set.why: The step back keeps this off the table as an order and puts it forward as something the speaker would prefer.

notice_set.sentence: I wish I could sleep through the traffic on the main road.
notice_set.question: Is the speaker sleeping through the traffic?
notice_set.why: Could is the stepped-back shape here, and it says the ability is missing rather than merely unused.

discovery.prompt: All three right-hand sentences are complaints about the same building. Work out what decides which one you reach for.
pairs: The lift is broken.
I wish the lift worked.
The caretaker never answers.
I wish the caretaker would answer.
Nobody reported the leak in March.
I wish somebody had reported the leak in March.

candidate_rules.text: The step back marks the gap; would appears only when the gap is somebody else's behaviour, and had only when the moment has gone.
Would is the polite version and the others are the blunt ones.
Use would whenever the sentence is about the future and had whenever it is about the past.

teach.rule_line: Ask what is missing: a state, a moment gone, or somebody else's habit.
teach.false_rule: That wish and would rather are polite ways of saying want. They say the thing is not happening, and want does not.

errors.wrong: I wish I have a garden big enough for a table.
errors.right: I wish I had a garden big enough for a table.
errors.why_it_happens: The sentence is about the here and now, so a present shape arrives on time and sounds right. Nothing in the way wish is usually taught says the step is where the meaning lives.
errors.smallest_fix: Swap one form: have becomes had.

errors.wrong: I wish the flat would be warmer in winter.
errors.right: I wish the flat were warmer in winter.
errors.why_it_happens: Would has been learned as the marker of wanting something changed, so it is attached to anything the speaker dislikes. Nobody is choosing to keep the flat cold, so there is no behaviour for would to point at.
errors.smallest_fix: Swap one form: would be becomes were.

errors.wrong: If only I would have kept the receipt for the boiler.
errors.right: If only I had kept the receipt for the boiler.
errors.why_it_happens: The learner reaches for would to mark the sentence as imaginary. Had plus the participle has already marked it, and the extra signal is what a reader trips over.
errors.smallest_fix: Swap one form: would have kept becomes had kept.
errors.l1_note: The doubled version circulates in informal speech, which keeps it sounding possible.

errors.wrong: It is time the lift is repaired properly.
errors.right: It is time the lift was repaired properly.
errors.why_it_happens: It is time reads like an ordinary statement about now, so the second half is built as one. The step back is the only thing that turns the sentence from a description into a complaint.
errors.smallest_fix: Swap one form: is becomes was.

pays_in.note: Any question about your home invites one of these frames within two sentences.
pays_in.model: I wish the kitchen had a bit more room, because two people in it is one too many.

pays_in.note: The reflective sentence at the end of a long turn usually needs one.
pays_in.model: Looking back, I wish I had asked more questions before I signed the agreement.

pays_in.note: It states an unmet need without turning the essay into a demand.
pays_in.model: It is high time planning rules treated small flats as homes rather than as investments.

pays_in.note: Complaints in a recorded conversation arrive in these shapes and are easy to mishear.
pays_in.model: I'd rather we sorted the deposit out before anybody moves anything in.

used_in.quote: The card asks what the speaker would change about the space they live in, which is this frame twice over.
The second half of the prompt asks what ought to be done, and an unmet need states itself most cleanly this way.

payload.sentence: I wish the flat had a balcony.
payload.question: Does the flat have a balcony?

feedback.why_key: The step backwards is doing all the work here. It says the balcony is missing while the sentence talks about the flat as it stands today.
feedback.feed_forward: Read a stepped-back verb after wish as a report of what is missing.

payload.sentence: I wish I had told her before she moved out.
payload.question: Which gap is the writer pointing at?
options: a chance that has already gone

feedback.why_key: Two steps back land on an occasion that is over, and the sentence reports the telling as something that never took place on it.
feedback.feed_forward: Count the steps back to find which moment is being called missing.

payload.context: Answering a question about where she lives and how far it is from the station.
payload.sentence: I wish I would live nearer the station.
reasons: would points at somebody else's behaviour, and this is about the speaker's own situation
the station has already closed
wish cannot be used about places
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: Where she lives is a state, not something she keeps choosing to do, so there is nothing for would to ask anybody to change.
feedback.feed_forward: Keep would for what other people keep doing.

payload.context: From a message about a north-facing front room. The speaker is describing how the room is today.
payload.stem: I wish the windows ___ (face) south, because the room never gets any sun.

feedback.why_key: The windows are where they are and nobody is going to turn them, so the sentence needs the shape that reports a state as wrong rather than a habit as annoying.
feedback.feed_forward: Step the verb back once for a state you cannot change.

payload.context: Written after the rate went up. The offer was open in March and closed in April.
payload.stem: If only we ___ (fix) the rate while the offer was open.

feedback.why_key: The offer closed, so the chance sits behind us, and the step goes one further back than the plain past to say nobody took it.
feedback.feed_forward: Use had plus the participle once the moment has closed.

payload.context: From a letter to the council about a street that has not been touched for eleven years.
payload.stem: It is high time somebody ___ (resurface) this road properly.

feedback.why_key: Nobody has started, and the step backwards is what turns a remark about the road into a complaint about the delay.
feedback.feed_forward: Step the verb back after it is high time.

payload.context: The caretaker has a phone on the desk and lets it ring. Build the complaint.

expected: i wish the caretaker would answer the phone

feedback.why_key: Would sits between the person and the thing you want them to do, which is why this shape only works when somebody else is the one not doing it.
feedback.feed_forward: Put would straight after the person who is not acting.

payload.given: The people upstairs keep dragging furniture around after midnight.
payload.instruction: Ask for it to stop, beginning with a wish rather than with a request.

expected: would stop dragging furniture around after midnight
wouldn't drag furniture around after midnight
would not drag furniture around after midnight
wouldnt drag furniture around after midnight

feedback.why_key: They are choosing to do it and could choose otherwise, which is exactly the gap this shape was built for.
feedback.feed_forward: Reach for would when the person could stop and has not.

payload.audio_text: I wish I'd said something while I had the chance.

expected: i wish i'd said something while i had the chance
i wish i had said something while i had the chance
i wish id said something while i had the chance

feedback.why_key: The 'd is a single consonant leaning on the pronoun, and a listener who loses it hears a complaint about now instead of a regret about then.
feedback.feed_forward: Listen for a d riding on the pronoun after wish.

payload.context: Two lines from separate messages about the same block of flats.
sentences: I wish the lift would work.
meanings: The lift is out of service and the writer is describing the building as it is.
The lift runs on some days and dies on others, and the writer wants it to behave.

feedback.why_key: One writer is reporting a broken thing; the other is asking a temperamental thing to sort itself out. Would is the only word carrying that difference.
feedback.feed_forward: Ask whether you are describing a state or asking for a change.

payload.context: From a complaint letter about a boiler that failed eleven months after it was fitted.
payload.sentence: I wish I would have kept the paperwork the engineer left.
reasons: the step backwards has already marked this as something that did not happen, so would has no work left
the paperwork is still valid
wish cannot be used about objects
nothing wrong, it's fine

feedback.why_key: Had plus the participle has already said the keeping did not happen. Adding would puts a second signal on one meaning, and readers hear the seam.
feedback.feed_forward: Delete would in front of had plus the participle.

payload.sentence: It is about time the council does something about the flooding on Brackenfield Row.

feedback.why_key: The council has done nothing, which is the whole point of the sentence, and the step backwards is where that impatience lives.
feedback.feed_forward: Step the verb back after it is about time.

payload.prompt_text: Think of one thing about the building or street you live on that somebody else could easily fix and has not. Write one sentence asking for it, without using the words please or should.

feedback.why_key: Naming somebody who could act and has not is the situation this shape exists for, and it makes the complaint land without an order in it.
feedback.feed_forward: Name the person who could act, then step the second verb back.

payload.prompt_text: You are asked about the space in your home and whether it is enough. In thirty seconds, give two sentences: one about a room as it is, and one about a change somebody else would have to make.

feedback.why_key: The two sentences need different shapes, and under time pressure the second one is where speakers reach for the first shape again and lose the request.
feedback.feed_forward: Switch shapes when you switch from a state to a person.
